items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: He said, Cus, do you think you can play with me tomorrow night? I said yeah. So I went on and played with him.

ctx.x: or nothing. And that's a bass player? You have any bass player? No, we didn't have any bass player.

No bass, piano? No piano player. I see. Well that's the first band I started playing with. After my uncle took me to Old Man's Shalow there. That was the first band. And on the way from that house I met Chris Kelly, he was playing Lawn Party and Faye Soda drummer, that was a guy I admired too, was a great drummer. And he asked me to help him carry his drum while he was playing. And so I was telling him, I was going to less and taking up drums. I'll let you work out tonight. So I got on the drum and started…
I thought maybe that song had something to do with Marcus Garvey, you know. No. Because he was a Jew maker too, you know.

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: So, that was one of the jobs that we stole away from Chris Kelly, because we started to play and we played several jobs and often for those people. And on those occasions, that's how I come to play with Chris Kelly and I played many advertisements, or truck jobs

ctx.x: That's right. We used to call it Going Home to Jamaica. So, from that night on, Chris Kelly decided to start to play, and I'm going home to Jamaica after that night. Because all those fellas, when they line them up and send them all back that didn't have their passport, back to Jamaica. So, this lady, she was so enthued over Lauren Stoker playing and being so young, that she sent for me to ask me could she get that little fella to play for her. So, that was one of the jobs that we stole away from Chris Kelly,…
Was he always pretty heavy? He was pretty heavy. Yeah, he always was.
